name: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED)
description: The St. Louis Fed's economic database: hundreds of thousands of series from U.S. government agencies, the Federal Reserve system and third parties, behind one REST API. This file lists only the families evaluated so far; any FRED series is reachable through the same access block — add a dataset here and an entry in catalog/research-log.md when one is evaluated. Series a third party owns under its own terms (S&P DJI, ICE BofA, University of Michigan) are catalogued under that rights holder with via: fred, not here.

notes: Request pattern: /fred/series/observations?series_id={id}&api_key={key}&file_type=json; file_type may be xml (default), json, xlsx or csv; frequency (d, w, m, q, a, …) and aggregation_method (avg, sum, eop) resample server-side.

All requests need an API key, issued through a FRED account (fredaccount.stlouisfed.org); the docs state no fee. This repo reads it from the FRED_API_KEY environment variable and calls the API through scripts/fred_utils.py.
A missing observation is the string '.', never zero; scripts/fred_utils.py drops it.

No numeric request limit is published; the API terms say the Bank may impose or adjust bandwidth and transaction limits. scripts/fred_utils.py retries on HTTP 429 and 5xx with exponential backoff, honouring Retry-After.
Series metadata (observation_start, frequency, units, notes) is available from /fred/series?series_id={id}; the dataset facts below were read from it on 2026-09-14.

Vintage (real-time) access: ALFRED (alfred.stlouisfed.org, 'Economic data time travel since 2006') exposes the same series at past revision states through the ordinary API — realtime_start/realtime_end (YYYY-MM-DD) is documented for /fred/series/observations and, per FRED's own realtime_period page, defaults to today on almost all FRED API URLs, selecting the data as known during that closed interval; /fred/series/vintagedates?series_id={id} lists the release dates a series was actually revised on (excludes releases where the data didn't change; up to 10,000 per call, paginated via limit/offset). No separate ALFRED API or key is needed — the FRED key and endpoints serve both. Not used by any fetcher in this repo as of 2026-09-15; this repo always reads current values (no realtime_start/realtime_end sent, i.e. 'today mode').

terms.summary: Public domain (U.S. government data) via FRED; attribution to FRED and the original source requested
terms.quote: Public Domain: Citation requested — These series may be under copyright or in the public domain and may be used without permission, provided you do not engage in any prohibited use. … Series with the following copyright labels—Public Domain: Citation requested and Copyrighted: Citation required—may be used for internal commercial uses and may be displayed in textbooks, newsletters, or reports to clients provided that appropriate attribution is given to FRED as well as the original source of the data.

datasets.name: Treasury constant-maturity yields, daily (H.15)
datasets.gives: Daily market yields on U.S. Treasury securities at constant maturities of 1, 3 and 6 months and 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20 and 30 years, from the Board of Governors' H.15 release, interpolated by the Treasury from its daily par yield curve
notes: Coverage start is DGS10's; tenors start later (DGS30 1977-02-15, DGS1MO 2001-07-31) and the 20- and 30-year tenors have a 2002–2006 gap that the yield-curve chart leaves visible.
Lag observed on 2026-09-14: Friday's value (2026-09-11) posted Monday afternoon.
Used by series/dgs10.json, series/yield_curve.json and series/spreads.json.

datasets.name: Treasury constant-maturity yields, monthly averages (H.15)
datasets.gives: Monthly averages of the daily constant-maturity yields at 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20 and 30 years, from the Board of Governors' H.15 release
roadmap: chart 4 (GS10 stitched to Shiller's pre-1953 long rate)
notes: GS10 and GS1 start 1953-04-01 (checked); other tenors not individually checked.
Lag observed: the August 2026 value was published 2026-09-01.

datasets.name: Treasury bill secondary-market rates, monthly (H.15)
datasets.gives: Monthly 3-month and 6-month Treasury bill secondary-market rates on a discount basis, from the Board of Governors' H.15 release
roadmap: chart 5 (ex-post real short rate: TB3MS minus CPI inflation)
notes: TB3MS starts 1934-01; TB6MS starts 1958-12.

datasets.name: TIPS constant-maturity real yields, daily (H.15)
datasets.gives: Daily market yields on Treasury inflation-indexed securities at constant maturities of 5, 7, 10, 20 and 30 years, from the Board of Governors' H.15 release
notes: DFII5 and DFII10 start 2003-01-02 (checked); DFII7, DFII20 and DFII30 start dates not checked.

datasets.name: Breakeven inflation rates, daily
datasets.gives: 10-year and 5-year breakeven inflation rates, computed by the St. Louis Fed as the nominal constant-maturity yield minus the TIPS yield at the same tenor

terms.summary: Copyrighted: Citation Required (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis) via FRED; usable with attribution to FRED

notes: FRED labels T10YIE 'Copyrighted: Citation Required' (source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, release: Interest Rate Spreads); FRED's legal page permits display with attribution for that label, so the terms override keeps the file's verified status and quote.
Published the same day (the 2026-09-14 value was present on 2026-09-14), so the lag is 0.

datasets.name: Effective federal funds rate, monthly and daily
datasets.gives: The effective federal funds rate as a monthly average (FEDFUNDS) and daily (DFF), from the Board of Governors' H.15 release
notes: FEDFUNDS is monthly from 1954-07; DFF is daily from 1954-07-01. FRED links a daily series for 1928–1954 in a separate category.

datasets.name: Secured Overnight Financing Rate, daily
datasets.gives: SOFR, the New York Fed's overnight Treasury repo rate, daily

datasets.name: Consumer Price Index, all urban consumers, monthly (BLS)
datasets.gives: CPI-U, all items, U.S. city average, seasonally adjusted, index 1982–1984 = 100, from the Bureau of Labor Statistics
notes: The FRED page does not state the release schedule; BLS publishes CPI around the middle of the following month (the August 2026 value was on FRED by 2026-09-11). Confirm against the BLS release calendar before setting a descriptor lag.
Seasonally adjusted; CPIAUCNS is the not-seasonally-adjusted counterpart.

datasets.name: NBER-based recession indicator, monthly
datasets.gives: A 0/1 monthly indicator built by the St. Louis Fed from the NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee's peak and trough months, trough method (the recession runs from the month after the peak through the trough month)
notes: Used by series/usrec.json, which collapses it to recession intervals for chart shading. The descriptor uses a lag of 5 business days for safety; observed: the August 2026 value was published 2026-09-01.
USRECM (midpoint method) and USRECP (peak method) are the other two interpretations FRED offers. NBER's own chronology is catalogued as nber/chronology.

datasets.name: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index, weekly
datasets.gives: The NFCI, a weekly index of U.S. financial conditions across money, debt and equity markets and the banking system; positive values mean tighter-than-average conditions

terms.summary: Copyrighted: Citation Required (Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago) via FRED; usable with attribution to FRED and the Chicago Fed

notes: FRED labels NFCI 'Copyrighted: Citation Required'; FRED's legal page permits display with attribution for that label, so the override keeps the file's verified status and quote.
Lag observed: the week ending Friday 2026-09-04 was published Wednesday 2026-09-10.

datasets.name: Cleveland Fed inflation expectations, monthly
datasets.gives: Model-based expected inflation at horizons of 1 to 30 years (one series per year), from the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland
notes: FRED labels EXPINF1YR 'Public Domain: Citation Requested'.
Published mid-month for the current month (the September 2026 value was on FRED by 2026-09-11), so relative to the period end the lag is 0.
One series per horizon, EXPINF1YR through EXPINF30YR; only the two listed endpoints were checked.

datasets.name: Treasury High Quality Market corporate bond spot-rate curve, monthly
datasets.gives: Spot rates for high-quality (AAA, AA, A) corporate bonds at each year of maturity from 1 to 30 years (projected to 100), from the U.S. Treasury's HQM yield curve
roadmap: item 11 (corporate rows of the yields table)
notes: FRED labels HQMCB10YR 'Public Domain: Citation Requested' (source: U.S. Department of the Treasury).
One series per year of maturity, HQMCB1YR through HQMCB30YR; only HQMCB1YR and HQMCB10YR were checked.
Lag observed: the August 2026 values were published 2026-09-04.

datasets.name: Moody's seasoned corporate bond yields, daily and monthly
datasets.gives: Seasoned Aaa- and Baa-rated corporate bond yields (20+ year maturities) from Moody's Investors Service: daily averages from the 1980s and monthly averages back to 1919

terms.summary: Copyrighted: Citation Required (Moody's Investors Service) via FRED; usable with attribution to FRED and Moody's
terms.quote: Public Domain: Citation requested — These series may be under copyright or in the public domain and may be used without permission, provided you do not engage in any prohibited use. … Series with the following copyright labels—Public Domain: Citation requested and Copyrighted: Citation required—may be used for internal commercial uses and may be displayed in textbooks, newsletters, or reports to clients provided that appropriate attribution is given to FRED as well as the original source of the data.

notes: All four series' badge (checked at the top of each series page, not the Notes section) reads 'Copyrighted: Citation Required', source 'Moody's'; FRED's legal page permits display with attribution for that label, so this dataset carries a verified terms override like NFCI and T10YIE, following the S8 precedent.
DAAA (Aaa, daily) starts 1983-01-03; DBAA (Baa, daily) starts 1986-01-02; AAA (Aaa, monthly) and BAA (Baa, monthly) both start 1919-01 — checked via the FRED API /fred/series endpoint on 2026-09-15.

Each series' own FRED 'notes' field (distinct from the usage-rights badge) carries Moody's own restrictive copyright boilerplate ('MAY NOT BE COPIED OR OTHERWISE REPRODUCED ... WITHOUT MOODY'S PRIOR WRITTEN CONSENT'), the same tension the S8 session already recorded for NFCI/T10YIE: FRED's own citation-required label is what governs display through FRED, per FRED's legal page.
Series cover only 20-year-and-above maturities per FRED's series notes; DAAA/DBAA are daily, AAA/BAA are monthly averages of the same underlying Moody's index.

datasets.name: Treasury term spreads, daily (10y−2y, 10y−3m)
datasets.gives: The 10-year minus 2-year and 10-year minus 3-month constant-maturity spreads, computed by the St. Louis Fed from Treasury data
notes: This repo computes its own spreads from the DGS legs (series/spreads.json) and uses these two series only as test oracles (tests/test_spreads.py); they are not chart inputs.
T10Y2Y starts 1976-06-01; T10Y3M starts 1982-01-04. Copyright label not checked; T10YIE, in the same Interest Rate Spreads release, is labelled Copyrighted: Citation Required.

notes: The FRED API Terms of Use require the notice 'This product uses the FRED® API but is not endorsed or certified by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis.' Every generated page carries it in a footer (scripts/build_site.py) since 2026-09-14.
The API terms prohibit using the API in connection with training machine-learning systems.

Third-party series: 'Before using data series owned by third parties for anything other than your own personal use, you must contact the data owner to obtain permission.' Those series are catalogued under their rights holder (spglobal for SP500; ICE BofA and the University of Michigan surveys when added), not here.
